title: Render on Linux with Vulkan, and fall back to the CPU
body:
This makes ff-unmute build and render on Linux. The GPU path uses Vulkan and a CPU fallback covers machines without a GPU.

**What changes**
- The Skia and native-player backend features move from the workspace into per-target dependencies: `metal` on macOS and `vulkan` everywhere else. `flat` and `lens` therefore build on Linux.
- A shared `tools/backend.rs` picks the backend from `FF_BACKEND`:
  - `auto` (default) tries the platform GPU and falls back to the CPU, printing that it did;
  - `gpu` fails if no GPU context can be created;
  - `cpu` never creates one.
- The CPU flat pass uses tiny-skia. The CPU lens pass uses Skia's raster context, so the SkSL lens shader still runs. Perspective, depth of field, palette, aberration, bloom, LED grid, tear and grain are all kept.
- `Cargo.lock` adds the Vulkan backend's dependencies.
- `tools/render.sh` validates `FF_BACKEND`, honours `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, and falls back to `uv run --with numpy --with scipy` when those packages are missing.
- The README lists the Linux requirements.
- `lens` gets a unit test that the lens SkSL compiles on the CPU path.

**Tested on Linux** (CachyOS, kernel 7.2, RTX 3080 Ti, NVIDIA Vulkan driver), with these results:
- `cargo test -p hud` and `cargo test --release -p flat -p lens --bins` pass.
- `FF_BACKEND=gpu tools/render.sh`: 480 frames, 30 fps, 1920x1080, 16.0 s, AAC audio. It took 357 s end to end.
- `FF_BACKEND=cpu tools/render.sh`, with every Vulkan ICD hidden: the same frame count, size and audio. It took 1384 s.
  - Against the GPU master the CPU master scores SSIM 0.80 and PSNR 26.9 dB. A 12-frame contact sheet matches frame for frame; the differences are antialiasing and filter softness.
- With the Vulkan ICDs hidden, both binaries fall back to the CPU under `FF_BACKEND=auto` and fail clearly under `FF_BACKEND=gpu`.
- `rustfmt --check` is clean on the changed files. `cargo clippy --no-deps -p flat -p lens --bins -- -D warnings` is clean.

**Not tested:** macOS (Metal) and Windows. Their code paths aren't meant to change, apart from the shared backend selection. `preview` still needs a GPU and a window; the fallback is for offline rendering only.

Opened as a draft. Thanks for the project, Mustafa!
